result.summary: Vendors an experimental secp256k1 batch verification module and integrates BIP 340 Schnorr signature batch verification into block validation. In both parallel and single-threaded validation within CCheckQueue, Taproot Schnorr signatures that miss the signature cache are queued and verified in batches via multi-scalar multiplication, falling back to individual verification if batch validation fails.
result.problem: Taproot Schnorr signatures are currently verified individually during block validation and initial block download. Individual verification incurs full per-signature elliptic curve point multiplication costs, missing the substantial verification throughput improvements offered by batch verification.
evidence: PR description and included secp256k1 documentation provide benchmark results and speedup plots showing significant verification time reductions per signature as batch sizes increase.
PR description notes the underlying secp256k1 implementation remains under review in bitcoin-core/secp256k1#1134 and bitcoin-core/secp256k1#1789.
result.scope_notes: A majority of the patch (+2,100 of +2,776 lines) consists of a vendored update to the src/secp256k1 subtree importing an unmerged batch verification module.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased the vendored secp256k1 subtree on updated upstream batch PR commits (incorporating API adjustments like void return types on add functions, sha256 hash context updates, and reset semantics) and added unit, functional, and CCheckQueue tests.
result.card: This pull request integrates BIP 340 Schnorr signature batch verification into Bitcoin Core block validation using an experimental libsecp256k1 batch verification module. Blocks currently verify each Taproot signature independently, missing the cryptographic throughput gains possible through multi-scalar multiplication batching during block connection and IBD. The PR imports an unmerged secp256k1 batch verification module and depends on upstream secp256k1 PRs #1134 and #1789.

risk.why: Flaws in signature batch verification or queue handling during block validation could cause nodes to accept invalid blocks or reject valid blocks, causing a consensus fork.
